title: Clear the String
explanation: Interval DP: s[l] is either deleted alone, or deleted together with a later equal character s[k] after clearing everything between them.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[l][r] = minimum operations to delete the whole substring s[l..r]
dp[i] = minimum operations to delete the prefix s[1..i]
options.why: Deleting the middle can merge characters from far apart; prefixes can't express that.

options.text: dp[l][r][c] = operations to delete s[l..r] leaving letter c
options.why: Unnecessary extra dimension; it can be done with plain dp[l][r].

options.text: Count maximal blocks of equal letters
options.why: That's an upper bound; merging blocks after removing the middle can do better.

extraLayers.explanation: Removals happen inside contiguous pieces, and n ≤ 500 allows O(n³): classic interval DP.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[l][r] = min(1 + dp[l+1][r], min over k ∈ (l, r] with s_k = s_l of dp[l+1][k−1] + dp[k][r])
dp[l][r] = min over k of dp[l][k] + dp[k+1][r]
options.why: Plain splitting never lets s[l] and s[k] disappear in the same operation.
Only works for palindromes-style matching; this problem allows any equal letter to join.
Always deletes s[l] alone; never merges.

extraLayers.explanation: Either s[l] is deleted on its own, or it rides along with the next copy of the same letter once the gap is cleared.
